case.summary: Transaction 3478561 is an online card-not-present purchase executed from a brand-new mobile device behind an anonymous proxy. That device is concurrently linked to 30 other cards, several of which were confirmed fraudulent in recent cases, indicating a coordinated compromise. The activity exactly matches the card_not_present_new_device pattern, and R6 further elevates concern due to the shared device across multiple cards. No other transactions on the card appear suspicious, so only 3478561 is flagged, but the connected card IDs should be monitored. Overall likelihood of fraud is high at approximately 85%.

sar.reason: R2/R6: fraud confirmed or strongly suspected with exposure $74.96. Shared device links to additional compromised cards. Policy threshold for regulatory filing met.
sar.narrative: On 22-Nov-2016, customer C13487, holder of debit card C13487-K1, attempted online transaction 3478561 in the amount of $74.96 at an e-commerce merchant while physically located unknown, as the activity originated from mobile device “SM-G935F Build/NRD90M” routed through an anonymous proxy. The device had no prior history with this customer but was simultaneously associated with at least 30 other cards, nine of which (IDs 12043, 11260, 23286, 21645, 11052, 15343, 22791, 19468, and 22867) are currently under fraud investigation or were confirmed compromised. The card-not-present activity precisely matches the bank’s “card_not_present_new_device” typology, indicating probable use of a stolen PAN rather than authorized customer action. Internal analytics assigned an 85 percent fraud probability and risk factor R6 because of the shared device linkage across multiple unrelated accounts. No additional suspicious activity was detected on C13487-K1 between 17-Oct-2016 and 22-Nov-2016; however, the connected cards exhibit elevated fraud indicators and remain under surveillance. The attempted transaction was declined, capping potential exposure at $74.96, and the customer was notified; no monetary loss has yet occurred. The convergence of a brand-new device, anonymized IP routing, broad multi-card usage, and overlap with known fraudulent cards renders the event highly suspicious for organized card-not-present fraud. Accordingly, the bank is filing this SAR to document the incident and facilitate further law-enforcement inquiry.
